title: New study reveals AI chatbots recognize unnecessary medical tests, but stumble where human doctors disagree
description: In an era where patients and clinicians increasingly turn to artificial intelligence for medical advice, a critical question emerges: Does AI know when not to test or treat? A new joint study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU) and Clalit Health Services reveals that leading large language models (LLMs) successfully identify when medical interventions are redundant in the vast majority of cases, stumbling primarily in gray areas where medical consensus itself is divided.

title: The AI is listening: Implications of machine-generated clinical notes on health care
description: Artificial intelligence tools are being touted as a solution for so-called pajama time—the time doctors inevitably spend compiling patient notes after working hours. As hospitals increasingly deploy AI scribes to listen and take notes during patient encounters, the data the scribes produce becomes the scaffold on which insights about health care, from billing to research to clinical decision-making, are built.
